evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-11-12"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-11-12". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is returned as a plain calendar date with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-03-01"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and dueDate null. PATCH /todos/3 with a new date changed it. PATCH /todos/1 with only a title kept the due date unchanged.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "13/11/2026" and "2026-11-13T10:00:00" each returned 400 with a JSON error body. PATCH with dueDate "2026-02-30" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today in UTC was 2026-11-13. A todo due 2026-11-12 had overdue=true. A todo due today had overdue=false. A todo due in 2027 had overdue=false. A todo with no due date had overdue=false. A todo due 2026-01-01 had overdue=true until it was marked done, then overdue=false. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the two open todos with past due dates (ids 1 and 3, after id 3's date was changed to 2026-05-05).
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed 'fällig 12.11.2026', 'fällig 13.11.2026', 'fällig 05.05.2026' and 'fällig 01.01.2026' next to the matching todos. The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the page, the two open todos with past due dates (past2, future with date 2026-05-05) showed the word 'überfällig'. The todo due today, the todo with no due date, and the done todo with a past due date showed no such marker.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only past2 and future, which are the overdue todos.
